title: [WT-13] Wrappers: control checkout follows the target; QA reviews landed bytes
description:
Plan against docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §6.

Objective: seats keep running the wrapper from committed main bytes. The control checkout sits on its own branch, moe/control, and fast-forwards to the target after every landing, so HEAD and the working files always move together and task-5998f871's committed-bytes reload is never deferred forever. QA only reviews a task whose landed commit the control checkout contains.

Deliverable, in scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 as twins:
- follow_control_checkout / Invoke-MoeControlFollow runs `git -C <control> -c core.hooksPath=<empty dir> merge --ff-only refs/heads/<target>`:
  - after L12 (L13);
  - at every loop top BEFORE the hot-reload check (wrapper_reload_deferred / Test-MoeWrapperReloadDeferred from task-5998f871e03d4ed5ab21f214073d85b2);
  - in the QA pre-flight after the claim.
- Branch states:
  - On the target or detached at the same commit: switch to moe/control, created at that commit if missing.
  - On another branch: MOE_CONTROL_NOT_FOLLOWING, no follow, one #general alert per hour.
  - A refused ff (local edits): MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_BEHIND, with git's file list and an hourly alert.
  - moe/control ahead of the target: MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_DIVERGED, alert; it is never reset.
  - Success: MOE_CONTROL_ADVANCED.
  - A follow failure never fails a landing.
- QA pre-flight: if the task's completion sha is not an ancestor of the control's HEAD after the follow, print MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_BEHIND, launch no CLI and call report_blocked.
- A wrapper whose own path is under <git top>/.worktrees/ refuses to start with MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE.
- Cases in scripts/tests/postflight.sh and postflight.ps1. Depends on WT-12 (task-06910296f63b4868849dc46cbb38a731) and task-5998f871.

NOT in scope: daemon dist rebuilds or restarts; worktree removal (WT-14); the §7.3 runbook text (WT-16); docs (WT-18).

Verification: node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh (and on a Windows seat: node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell)
definitionOfDone: postflight case (both harnesses): after a worktree landing, the control checkout on moe/control has HEAD == target and a clean `git status -- scripts/` (the wrapper file on disk equals HEAD's blob), and MOE_CONTROL_ADVANCED is printed.
postflight case: with a changed scripts/moe-agent.sh landed on the target, the next loop top follows first and the hot-reload check sees no uncommitted wrapper edit (no deferral line).

postflight cases: control on main at the target commit switches to moe/control; on another branch prints MOE_CONTROL_NOT_FOLLOWING; a local edit to a landed file prints MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_BEHIND; a local commit on moe/control prints MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_DIVERGED and is not reset.

postflight case: a QA claim whose completion sha is not in the control HEAD prints MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_BEHIND, launches no CLI and calls report_blocked; a wrapper started from .worktrees/<id>/scripts/ prints MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE and exits non-zero.
Existing postflight and worktree-landing cases pass unchanged; both wrappers carry the same MOE_WORKTREE_/MOE_LAND_/MOE_CONTROL_/MOE_BOARD_ codes; the verification command exits 0.

implementationPlan.description: 1. Reject execution of wrappers from task worktrees (tests first). Goal: seats use committed control-checkout wrapper bytes; normal shared launches and bundled non-Git wrappers remain unchanged. Architecture: startup guard on wrapper identity; control-follow only in worktree operation; QA checks the served completion after follow. Tech: Git/Bash/Python and PS5.1. Read revised design §6 and landed WT-12/WT-04 mode/target seams; do not reimplement them. Add a guard before daemon/config/claim side effects using the actual wrapper source path (BASH_SOURCE / PSCommandPath), not current cwd, --project or MOE_WORKTREE_PATH. Canonicalize source and its own Git checkout/common repository location; if the source is inside that repository's reserved .worktrees/<id>/ subtree, including a linked-worktree root or symlink/junction alias, print MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE and exit nonzero. Distinguish a real path-component descendant from names like .worktrees-other; do not reject an unrelated project merely because an ancestor elsewhere has that spelling. Non-Git bundled wrapper is not falsely treated as a task worktree. Use argument arrays/literal paths and the existing Windows/WSL normalization with ordinal comparisons, preserving POSIX case. Twin cases: actual registered task worktree wrapper refuses even with --project control or cwd outside W; symlink alias where supported; control and non-Git bundled wrapper still launch; path with spaces; assert zero claim/daemon-start/CLI calls on refusal.
implementationPlan.note:
Guard added before any side effect. sh: moe_wrapper_in_worktree, right after SCRIPT_DIR. ps1: a scriptblock after the -Loop/-NoLoop check, with local EAP Continue and try/catch.
- It uses git's physical paths: show-toplevel, show-prefix, and the first `worktree list` entry.
- It refuses when the prefix starts with .worktrees/task-*, or when top is <main>/.worktrees/task-x, i.e. a registered W.
- Paths are case-folded on msys/Windows; comparisons are Ordinal everywhere else.
- A failed git call (non-Git bundled copy) launches.

Test: new postflight-worktree.cjs case wt-guard, plus opts.wrapper on launch(). Scope growth: this cjs is the one worktree suite both harnesses run.
- Refused: a registered task worktree copy and a symlink/junction alias, both with --project control and cwd outside W, under a root path with a space. Each exits 1 with no RPC and no CLI.
- Launched: a .worktrees-other/task-* copy and a non-Git bundled copy.

Filed task-3c4be125 (bug): from inside a worktree-mode W, the harnesses launch W's own wrapper and would be refused.

implementationPlan.description: 2. Implement follow_control_checkout / Invoke-MoeControlFollow with non-destructive branch handling and error handling. These are NEW twin helpers. Use explicit control root/target and local Git variables so worktree landing globals are not overwritten. Enable from the effective worktree mode (project mode for control seats, pinned mode for a worker attempt); shared attempts stay on their existing path. Resolve target using the landed literal consolidationBranch-or-main rule. Read HEAD and target as commits and symbolic branch. On refs/heads/moe/control proceed. On the target branch, or detached HEAD exactly at target, create moe/control at that same HEAD using hooks-off git switch -c if absent, or switch to it only if its existing tip equals current HEAD; never -C/-f, never reuse a different existing tip. On another branch or switch failure print MOE_CONTROL_NOT_FOLLOWING and leave every ref/file unchanged. For moe/control, require `git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD refs/heads/<target>`: exit 1 (ahead OR diverged) gives MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_DIVERGED, other errors refuse without guessing. Equal tips are an idempotent no-op. Before advancing ensure the proposed ff does not change .moe paths; runtime state must remain daemon-owned. Run exactly `git -C <control> -c core.hooksPath=<owned empty dir> merge --ff-only refs/heads/<target>`. Success with HEAD movement prints MOE_CONTROL_ADVANCED; failure prints MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_BEHIND plus bounded Git stderr/file list. Never reset, stash, force, delete a lock, stage board files or clean human dirt. Re-read HEAD after contention so a peer's completed follow can count as an already-current no-op, not false divergence. Twin tests: main->new/existing-same moe/control, detached-at-target, ordinary ff with HEAD==target and disk script==HEAD blob, already-current, unrelated branch, mismatched existing moe/control, ahead/diverged control, conflicting local edit/untracked file, Git-lock/refusal and dirty .moe sentinels preserved. A failure must not modify the published target.
implementationPlan.note:
Added follow_control_checkout [switch] / Invoke-MoeControlFollow [-Switch] and control_alert / Send-MoeControlAlert, placed after control_worktree_mode / Test-MoeControlWorktreeMode.

How the follow works:
- Target: literal consolidationBranch, else main (pattern characters → main), the same rule as the landing.
- Off moe/control it returns, unless called with switch. With switch, a HEAD on the target or detached at the target's commit switches with hooks off: `switch -c moe/control` when the branch is absent, `switch --no-guess moe/control` only when it is at that same commit. Anything else gives MOE_CONTROL_NOT_FOLLOWING.
- HEAD is read before the target tip. Equal tips are a no-op.
- `merge-base --is-ancestor`: rc 1 → DIVERGED (covers ahead too); any other non-zero → BEHIND.
- A target diff that touches `<rel>.moe` → BEHIND (daemon-owned paths).
- Then `git -C <top> -c core.hooksPath=<empty> merge -q --ff-only --no-autostash refs/heads/<target>`. Failure → BEHIND with up to 1500 characters of git stderr (the file list included). If the merge failed but a re-read HEAD already contains the tip (a peer's follow won), it is a silent no-op. Success → `[OK] MOE_CONTROL_ADVANCED old..new`.
- It never resets, stashes, forces, cleans, or deletes a lock. It always returns, so the caller goes on.

Alerts: a [WARN] line on every call; a #general chat at most once an hour per code, via an epoch stamp at <gitdir>/moe/control-alert-<CODE>.

Wiring: the worker provision call site (`follow_control_checkout switch` before WT-04's moe/control check) is done in this step, because the tests drive it.

Tests (new cjs case wt-follow, 14 branch states, one worker pre-flight each): switch-new, switch-same, detached, current, advance (disk scripts/ == HEAD blob), moe-dirt preserved, feature, mc-elsewhere, ahead, diverged, edit, untracked, lock (index.lock kept), and moe-landed. Each asserts the exact MOE_CONTROL_ code set, the HEAD ref and sha, that main is unmoved, and refused-or-launched.

Changed one existing refusal row: 'control' now uses a feature branch instead of `switch main`. Under §6.5, main at the target's commit now auto-switches.

Results:
- sh `wt-follow,control,codes`: all ok.
- Windows PowerShell 5.1 via Windows node, `wt-follow,control,codes`: 3 ok, 0 failed.

implementationPlan.description: 3. Wire all follow sites and bounded operator alerts. Invoke the helper (a) after successful completion L12 as L13, (b) at every loop top after polling and BEFORE wrapper hash/committed-byte reload checks, including first iteration, (c) after a QA claim/context fetch before launch. Ensure initial loop follow/auto-switch happens before WT-04's worker moe/control prerequisite check; a human feature branch remains WT-04's report_blocked/no-W path. Preserve wrapper_reload_deferred/Test-MoeWrapperReloadDeferred, syntax checks, deferred-hash logic and reload/deregister flow unchanged, including Bash's grouped-loop exit fence. L13 failure is warning-only and cannot alter C's committed/landed outcome or re-finalize it as failed. For NOT_FOLLOWING/BEHIND/DIVERGED, send one #general alert per hour across seats of this control checkout, naming root/target/code and preserving Git's useful path list without unbounded output. Keep shared throttle state under the common Git directory, not .moe; a small exclusive-create/mkdir guard around read/update of a UTC-epoch timestamp is sufficient. Concurrent callers skip a held alert lock; notification/metadata failure never blocks follow or landing, and cleanup is in finally. No sleeping/spinning on another seat. Test the L13 result stays landed under follow refusal; two callers/repeated loop warnings generate at most one chat row inside an hour, then another after a fixture-adjusted timestamp (no real hour sleep); hooks never run during switch/ff. Add a committed target-only wrapper change to the existing reload scratch fixture: next loop follows before hash comparison, source equals HEAD and no MOE_WRAPPER_RELOAD_DEFERRED appears; unchanged shared reload cases still pass.
implementationPlan.note: Follow sites wired per comment 1e3e602a. (a) L13: the worktree post-flight runs follow_control_checkout / Invoke-MoeControlFollow after a committed|nothing completion, after the board snapshot. It only warns and never changes the landed outcome; the wt-follow-sites L13 row proves a BEHIND refusal leaves the completion committed and finalize landed. (b) The loop top runs while HEAD is exactly refs/heads/moe/control, after ACCOUNT_RELAUNCH reset and BEFORE the MOE_WRAPPER_LAUNCH_HASH / Test-MoeWrapperReloadDeferred check. Reload, deferral and syntax logic are unchanged. (c) The worker auto-switch runs only in provision_worktree / Initialize-MoeWorktree when workspace.mode is worktree, before WT-04's moe/control head check, so a feature branch still gets WT-04's NOT_FOLLOWING/report_blocked path. The QA pre-flight runs qa_control_preflight / Invoke-MoeQaControlPreflight only on moe/control: sync_land_target in remote mode first, then the follow. A control seat off moe/control (shared mode) runs and alerts nothing (wt-follow shared-work case on moe/work-2026-11-02). Alerts (NOT_FOLLOWING/BEHIND/DIVERGED): [WARN] line, plus one #general row per code per hour across seats. State is <common gitdir>/moe/control-alert-<CODE> (UTC epoch), guarded by an exclusive-create control-alert.lock. A held lock means the alert is skipped with no spin or sleep; a lock older than 10 min is reclaimed; cleanup is in finally/rm. Git's error text is capped at 1500 chars. Throttle tested: runs 1, 2, 3 (backdated stamp), held, stale; #general rows go 1,1,2,2,3. Hooks never run on switch/ff (a GUID temp hooksPath; every wt-follow case installs post-checkout/post-merge markers). Intended behaviour change: wt-completion / wt-hooks now assert controlFollowed (HEAD == main after landing, status clean) instead of controlSame, which is L13 by design. The 'control' refusal row now uses a feature branch, since main at the target now switches. Hot-reload follow arm added to postflight.sh and postflight.ps1. Verified: sh wt-follow, wt-follow-sites, wt-completion, wt-hooks 4 ok; ps1 (PS5.1) wt-follow, wt-follow-sites, wt-completion, wt-hooks, control, codes 6 ok; sh reload-follow arm ok (crc); ps1 reload-follow arm ok (crc, scratch extraction); parity-check PASS; bash -n ok. implementationPlan.description: 4. Gate QA launch on the actual recorded completion's ancestry. Read `task.landing.lastCompletion.sha` from the claimed task's served context (verified getContext.ts buildLanding field), not a checkpoint, rescue SHA, task branch tip or arbitrary HEAD. After control follow, validate it as a commit and run `git -C <control> merge-base --is-ancestor <completionSha> HEAD`. Exit 0 permits QA, including a later target containing C; absent/invalid/unavailable SHA or nonzero Git result prints MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_BEHIND with the task/SHA/reason, launches no CLI and calls report_blocked for that claimed task. Use the existing preflight-block path and identity; on RPC failure still do not launch or fall through to taskless QA, and report the failed acknowledgement. Leave actual task status/ownership changes to Moe. In the worktree QA prompt name the review commit and `git diff <sha>^ <sha>` so a later HEAD is not mistaken for this task's diff. Do not change shared-mode QA behavior. Add a conditional lastCompletion projection to the ONE shared postflight-fake-proxy.js using explicit test fixture input/task record; unset remains today's payload and no production daemon edit is needed. Twin tests: C absent while follow is refused -> code, exactly one report_blocked and no fake CLI; C becomes ancestor after ff -> launch; C is an ancestor of later HEAD -> launch; malformed/missing SHA and Git error -> no launch; task checkpoint must not satisfy the check; shared fixture unchanged.
implementationPlan.note: QA landed-bytes gate. qa_landed_gate (sh) / Assert-MoeQaLandedCommit (ps1) run right after the QA control pre-flight, only when HEAD is refs/heads/moe/control, so shared-mode QA is unchanged. The gate reads get_context task.landing.lastCompletion.sha (the daemon's buildLanding field), which must be a string of exactly 40 lowercase hex chars. A checkpoint, rescue ref or branch tip is never consulted. Then `git cat-file -e sha^{commit}` and `git merge-base --is-ancestor sha HEAD`. Any failure goes through the existing worktree_stop / Stop-MoeWorktreeSeat path: [ERROR] MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_BEHIND naming the task, sha and reason (rc included), one report_blocked, no CLI, exit 1. A failed report_blocked still stops with its WARN. On pass the gate appends to the dynamic context 'Review commit <C>: ... Its diff is 'git diff <C>^ <C>'; HEAD may be later...'. Fake proxy: a new FAKE_CTX_LANDING JSON-object knob sets task.landing; unset leaves the payload unchanged. The existing QA launches (wt-control-seats qa, wt-board-qa/off, wt-qa-remote) now pass landed(<sha in HEAD>), as a real daemon would. New case wt-qa-gate: C behind a refused follow -> refused, HEAD unmoved; ff onto C -> launch and the prompt names C once plus its diff; C under a later HEAD D -> launch naming C; none / checkpoint-only at HEAD / 12-char / uppercase / unknown 40-hex / stubbed --is-ancestor failure -> refused with the matching reason; shared moe/work branch -> launch, no MOE_CONTROL_ code, no review line. RED: wt-qa-gate failed on sh before the gate ('no [ERROR] MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_BEHIND: line'). GREEN: sh wt-qa-gate, wt-control-seats, wt-board, wt-follow-sites 4 ok; ps1 (PS5.1) same 4 ok; parity-check PASS. Other control-checkout harnesses (worktree-landing, postflight wtr, worktree-e2e) launch workers only, so none of them needs the knob.

implementationPlan.note: Adversarial self-review of the full WT-13 diff. FIXED (real): the follow checked old..tip for daemon-owned .moe paths but then merged refs/heads/<target>, which can move between check and merge. Both wrappers now merge the verified $tip sha. New case wt-follow-race: the git stub holds the loop top's --ff-only while the test lands .moe/landed.json on main. It asserts ADVANCED old..tip, HEAD == tip, no .moe/landed.json on disk, and the pre-flight follow's BEHIND 'daemon-owned' line. RED proven on sh by temporarily restoring the ref merge (HEAD went past tip). GREEN sh 8 ok and ps1 PS5.1 8 ok (wt-follow-race, wt-follow, wt-follow-sites, wt-completion, wt-hooks, wt-qa-gate, control, codes). The ps1 reload-follow arm was re-run ok. commitOn() gained an optional base (default HEAD, existing callers unchanged). Named bash gate re-run on the final bytes: exit 0, failureClass NONE, worktree-landing 18/18, parity PASS. CONSIDERED, theoretical: (a) A human switching branches between the symbolic-ref read and the merge could ff their own branch. ff-only loses no commits and the window is two git calls. (b) Two seats reclaiming the same stale (>10 min) alert lock at once can send 2 rows in an hour. (c) Two concurrent follows: index.lock makes one fail; if HEAD already contains tip it is silent (lock case covered). (d) Ahead and diverged both report DIVERGED (rc 1). (e) Target checked out elsewhere is untouched; only moe/control's HEAD moves. (f) moe/control collision at another commit gives NOT_FOLLOWING (mc-elsewhere); --no-guess means no remote DWIM. (g) Guard: physical paths, so a junction/symlink alias is caught; case-insensitive on Windows; .worktrees-other passes; a non-Git copy launches. (h) Alert clock in the future is treated as old, so the alert is sent and the stamp rewritten; lock/stamp IO failures never block. (i) QA reads only lastCompletion: checkpoint-only, malformed, unknown or rescue shas all fail closed. CONFIRMED: main/target is never written by the follow. The QA remote pre-flight's sync_land_target mirrors origin's target into the local ref, as comment e6073e9d requires. Human dirt and .moe are never discarded (no reset/stash/clean, --no-autostash). L13 runs after the landing and board snapshot and only warns. The follow precedes the hot-reload hash check and WT-04's head check. Loop/parser/reload code is unchanged; held-out worktree-landing.{sh,ps1} are unchanged vs 8ad04de7. OVER BUDGET: about 640 net LOC versus the plan's 400, roughly 340 wrappers and 320 tests. The twin tests the plan enumerates account for most of it; nothing was cut to fit.

comments.author: worker-0062feec
comments.content:
Spike self-review correction for rail 4 (docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §6.1, §6.2, §6.4, §6.5; section numbers unchanged). Where this differs from the description, this comment wins.

1. The follow runs in three places only:
   - at L13;
   - in a worker or QA pre-flight, after a claim whose workspace.mode is `worktree`;
   - at the loop top, but ONLY while HEAD is refs/heads/moe/control.
   A loop top on any other branch does nothing: no follow, no switch, no MOE_CONTROL_NOT_FOLLOWING alert. In shared mode that branch is moe/work-<date>, or main in a main-direct project. Add a case: a loop top on moe/work-<date> prints no MOE_CONTROL_ code and leaves HEAD alone.
2. So the auto-switch and the NOT_FOLLOWING alert happen only after a worktree-mode claim or at L13. Your DoD cases "control on main switches" and "another branch prints NOT_FOLLOWING" run after such a claim.
3. MOE_CONTROL_ADVANCED <old>..<new> is printed when the follow moves HEAD.
4. In remote mode, the QA pre-flight runs sync_land_target (L4's fetch and mirror) before the follow, so a commit landed from another clone is in the control checkout's HEAD.
5. MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE fires only inside <git top>/.worktrees/task-*. The using-git-worktrees skill and humans keep their own worktrees under .worktrees/, and two such directories exist today.

comments.author: worker-0062feec
comments.content:
Correction to my comment e6073e9d, points 1 and 2 (design doc §6.2/§6.5/§7.2 updated to match). A QA or architect claim always records workspace.mode 'shared' (WT-01's contract), so the QA pre-flight cannot gate on its claim.

- The follow runs:
  - at L13;
  - in a WORKER pre-flight after a claim whose workspace.mode is 'worktree' (the only place the auto-switch and MOE_CONTROL_NOT_FOLLOWING can fire);
  - in the QA pre-flight and at every loop top, only while the control checkout is in worktree mode, i.e. HEAD is exactly refs/heads/moe/control.
- Reuse WT-07's predicate, sh control_worktree_mode / ps1 Test-MoeControlWorktreeMode (Serena decision-worktree-control-seat-mode-signal, #general msg-46da6ff7). Any git failure counts as shared.
- For a control seat, a HEAD off moe/control means shared mode: nothing runs and nothing alerts (rail 4).
- Points 3-5 stand.
